title: FREQUENCY ZERO
screenplayText:
TITLE: FREQUENCY ZERO
FORMAT: Short Film (12 Pages)
AUTHOR: Zaeem Khan

SCENE 1
INT. K-DESERT BROADCAST BOOTH - NIGHT [1 4/8 PAGES]
A smoke-hazed 1970s radio studio lost in the Nevada expanse. Amber VU meters dance to silence. 
JACK (50s, bloodshot eyes, unlit cigarette behind his ear) leans into an RCA ribbon microphone.
MAYA (20s, grease-smudged knuckles, headphones around her neck) watches through the glass from the master rack.

JACK
(into mic)
Three-fourteen in the morning, high desert. You're on Frequency Zero. If anybody's breathing out past Mile Marker 80... you're not alone.

Jack drops a needle onto a battered acetate record. A strange HIGH-FREQUENCY WHINE pierces the monitor speakers.

MAYA
Jack, cut the feed! That signal isn't coming from our relay tower.

JACK
Where's it pulling from, Maya?

MAYA
(checking oscilloscope)
It's bouncing off the ionosphere... but the time-code header is stamped twenty-four hours ahead. Tomorrow night.

scriptParse.title: FREQUENCY ZERO
scriptParse.logline: When an isolated graveyard-shift desert radio DJ intercepts an impossible broadcast from 24 hours in the future predicting a fatal highway collapse, he must risk everything on live air to stop an oncoming night freight convoy.

scenes.summary: DJ Jack Mercer hosts his late-night broadcast when engineer Maya detects an impossible future-dated audio broadcast bouncing off the ionosphere.
Maya and Jack battle a sparking, smoking 50k-watt transmitter coil that threatens to ignite the station.
Jack steps beneath the tower in the howling wind and hears his own voice reporting his death on tomorrow's broadcast.
Jack and Maya explain the prophetic broadcast to a skeptical Deputy Reyes at first light.
Maya rigs emergency transmitter frequencies while Jack plots the doomed freight truck's route on a map.
Jack drives to the highway checkpoint and learns from road workers that bridge inspections were postponed.
At dusk, Jack discovers sheared structural rivets on the canyon bridge span and radios Maya as the storm hits.
In a raging rainstorm, Jack flags down the runaway freight truck with a flare and dives across the guardrail to survive the skid.
An injured, bandaged Jack returns to the microphone to close the broadcast as the future timeline resets.
Jack and Maya share coffee on the truck tailgate at sunrise as the station broadcasts into a peaceful new morning.

coverage.logline: When an isolated graveyard-shift desert radio DJ intercepts an impossible broadcast from 24 hours in the future predicting a fatal highway collapse, he must risk everything on live air to stop an oncoming night freight convoy.
coverage.synopsis: Set in a remote 1970s Nevada broadcast station, FREQUENCY ZERO opens on veteran night-shift DJ Jack Mercer and his sharp young engineer Maya detecting a rogue radio transmission stamped 24 hours in the future. As the future audio details a catastrophic gorge collapse claiming Jack's own life, Jack and Maya scramble to warn local authorities before embarking on a dangerous race against time. Jack reaches the canyon bridge during a violent desert storm, risking his life with a magnesium flare to stop an oncoming freight semi-truck from plummeting into the abyss, successfully altering the timeline before returning to sign off his final morning broadcast.

strengths: Auditory-driven high concept that maximizes low-budget indie production value
Compelling dynamic between weary DJ Jack and engineer Maya
Contained physical locations allowing high-craft lighting and acoustic design
concerns: Scene 8 night rain bridge sequence demands precise stunt and rain rig coordination
coverage.pacingNotes: Exemplary three-act escalation within 12 pages. The mystery hook is established in scene 1, investigative rising tension carries through scenes 2-7, and scene 8 delivers an explosive physical climax.
coverage.verdictRationale: A masterclass in contained, high-concept narrative economy. FREQUENCY ZERO pairs an indelible sonic hook with airtight production pragmatism, making it an extraordinary festival contender and feature proof-of-concept.
coverage.pullQuote: An electrifying masterclass in analog audio suspense.

pitchKit.tagline: Tomorrow's disaster is tonight's last broadcast.
loglines: When an isolated graveyard-shift desert radio DJ intercepts an impossible broadcast from 24 hours in the future predicting a fatal highway collapse, he must risk everything on live air to stop an oncoming night freight convoy.
A late-night radio DJ hears his own fatal obituary broadcast twenty-four hours ahead of time.
One booth, one microphone, and a race against tomorrow's headline.

pitchKit.pitchParagraph: Carrying an Ink Story Analyst coverage verdict of RECOMMEND and an audited Ledger production budget of $31,875 across a 4-day shoot, FREQUENCY ZERO is an airtight, high-ROI proof-of-concept for theatrical and episodic sci-fi suspense. By grounding its supernatural temporal premise in tangible 1970s analog radio hardware and visceral physical stunts, the project delivers A-list festival production value with disciplined indie capital efficiency.
